learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the physical and technological fundamentals of the main industrial manufacturing processes.
Identify, classify, and apply the different mechanical technologies and machine tools available for manufacturing materials of various natures (metallic and non-metallic).
Be able to evaluate and select the most appropriate and efficient manufacturing technological process for obtaining a specific product, considering design and material criteria.
Acquire adequate notions about the fundamentals, instruments, and methods of general metrology applied to quality control in manufacturing.

syllabus_topics: Manufacturing Processes by Fusion and Consolidation (Molding and Powder Metallurgy)
Machining Manufacturing Processes (Chip Removal) and Finishing
Mechanical Forming and Joining Processes (Deformation, Cutting and Welding)
Non-Metallic Material Processing Technologies and Prototyping
Applied Process Engineering and Production Cycle Analysis

assessment_methods.method: In-class challenges with AI and debates

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as a weighted average of two blocks: Participation in Seminars (10%) and the Theoretical-Practical Final Exam (90%). A minimum score of 5.0 out of 10 is required on the individual theoretical-practical exam (which accounts for 60% of the 90% block) to average with the other parts. The 90% block is diversified into an individual theoretical-practical exam (60%), a group integrative project (20%), and in-class challenges with AI and debates (10%). Students can opt for a single final written exam, covering 100% of the theoretical, practical, and seminar aspects, by formally requesting it in writing at least 20 calendar days before the official exam date.
